bullets.title: MU: Consensus bullish into Wed earnings; DRAM +45% ASPs, $28-30 EPS target, SCAs key focus
bullets.body: Street-wide consensus is strongly bullish on Micron ahead of Wednesday's report: MS models DRAM ASPs up 45% q/q (vs 40% prior), NAND up 50%, with $21.31 EPS vs $20.57 consensus; GS estimates ~$48.7B revenue and $29.95 EPS (vs street $23.70); Jefferies targets ~$30 EPS for the August print and ~$200 for CY27. Buyside (~75%) expects additional Strategic Customer Agreements (SCAs) covering 30-50% of forward bit shipments. MU is up ~168% YTD and accounts for 17% of S&P 500 YTD gains; crowded positioning (heightened LTA concentration risk) is flagged as a messaging risk.

bullets.title: MU/WDC/SNDK/STX: Memory pricing super-cycle — 40-50% 3Q, 30-40% 4Q surge expected
bullets.body: Memory contract prices are projected to rise 40-50% q/q in 3Q26 and 30-40% in 4Q26 per memory consultants, following ~40% gains in 2Q26. WDC +32.6% last week, MU +15.5%, SNDK +4.2%, STX +3.4% in pre-market. Fox Advisors downgraded both STX and WDC to equal-weight from outperform on valuation after the run; UBS prefers the memory/HDD supply chain over hyperscalers/software. Memory industry LTAs now only with CSPs at ~50% of capacity, limiting consumer electronics supply and reinforcing pricing discipline.

bullets.title: ACN: Crashes 18-25% on weak bookings, guidance cut — TD Cowen downgrades to Hold, PT $150
bullets.body: Accenture's FY3Q26 bookings missed Visible Alpha consensus by 7% at -3% cc; FY26 revenue guidance cut to 3-4% from 3-5%; large Managed Services deals pushed to FY27. TD Cowen downgraded ACN to Hold from Buy, slashing PT to $150 from $258. UBS's Kevin McVeigh maintains Buy at $275 PT. The miss reignites AI disintermediation concerns across IT Services, and the stock is down ~52% YTD.

bullets.title: CRDO: Evercore ISI initiates Outperform at $325; Roth maintains Buy at $300 on AI infrastructure ramp
bullets.body: Evercore ISI initiated CRDO at Outperform with a $325 target (analyst Mark Lipacis), citing broad AI infrastructure connectivity opportunity. Roth separately reaffirmed its Buy/$300 PT following ROTH London Conference meetings, noting optical business expected to contribute at least $600M revenue this fiscal year and ZF optical module gaining meaningful customer traction. CRDO gained +5.3% in pre-market on the Evercore initiation.

bullets.title: COHR: CEO meetings confirm CPO on track, InP capacity to 4x by CY27, gross margin target >42%
bullets.body: JPM (Overweight) reports CEO investor meetings confirmed datacom TRx pricing is healthy with demand exceeding supply; 1.6T ramping before 800G peaks; CPO scale-out on track for C2H26, scale-up C2H27. InP capacity will double by C3Q26 and double again in CY27 (4x in two years), with 6-inch yields tracking ahead. Gross margin target >42% with potential reset higher driven by price optimization, 6-inch shift, and margin-accretive new products (CPO, OCS, multi-rail). OCS SAM now estimated at $4B, potentially conservative.

bullets.title: FOXA/ROKU: FOXA down ~24% post-Roku bid; JPM sees deal at 22x peak EBITDA as richly priced
bullets.body: Fox agreed to acquire Roku at ~$160/share (~22x FY27E EBITDA on peak growth), levering to 2.8x net. FOXA stock fell ~20-24% on deal announcement. Pre-deal FOXA traded at ~8x FY27E EBITDA; pro forma it functions as a ROKU proxy. Wolfe downgraded ROKU to Peer Perform. NFLX withdrew from bidding per Semafor. Analyst Supino argues FOXA trades within its 2-year standalone EV/EBITDA range on a pro forma basis and notes strong 2026 upfront commitments (HSD% growth, 8 of 10 largest advertiser categories up YoY).

bullets.title: APP: Citi removes upside catalyst watch; eComm client count slips 2% WoW in Week 25
bullets.body: Citi removed its 90-day positive catalyst watch on APP, citing a slower-than-expected ramp in eCommerce clients following Axon GA — management is prioritizing measured onboarding over rapid expansion. Week 25 data shows eCommerce clients fell 2% WoW to 10,282, driven by a 13% drop in Hong Kong stores (viewed as one-off). QTD average weekly store growth decelerated from 3.1% in 1Q26 to 2.3% in 2Q26. APP eComm channel remains strong for DTC but no near-term client inflection now expected.

bullets.title: ANET/CSCO: MS prefers networking over optical; ANET gaining share in backend switches, CSCO up 8 pts YoY
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes networking (ANET/CSCO) gaining momentum with inference opportunity ahead of earnings, while optical stocks are down ~10% YTD. In backend switches, ANET gained ~3 pts YoY to 12% share; CSCO gained significantly (+8 pts) to ~13% within top cloud customers. CLS holds #1 position with >25% share as the only vendor shipping early 1.6T volumes. 800G dominates at ~80% of Ethernet backend revenue; 1.6T expected to ramp in 2H with Amazon/Google first, Meta in 1H27.

bullets.title: GLW/LITE/COHR: MS prefers GLW in optical; Source Photonics $1.2B expansion pressures LITE/COHR margins
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley sees GLW as the cleanest optical story, supported by Fujikura's FY outlook raise (+47% operating profit). LITE and COHR face margin headwinds from Source Photonics' announced $1.2B optical chip/module expansion (5-6x potential capacity growth), creating competitive pressure on CW laser pricing. Wolfe Research notes AI-related optical stocks down 5-20% past month on InP oversupply from China, CPO timing concerns, and valuation.

bullets.title: SNAP: AR 'Specs' launch flops; stock -10% on mass-market skepticism
bullets.body: Snap launched AR glasses 'Specs' priced at $2,195 last week; the stock traded down ~10-11% on market skepticism about mass-market appeal. JPM describes the product as 'heavy, niche enthusiast' unlikely to succeed unless the core ad business turns around. Mizuho is hosting expert calls on social media litigation risks (mental health/minors) for SNAP, META, and GOOGL.

bullets.title: SNOW: UBS Buy/$370 PT maintained; AI pass-through revenues immaterial (~1%) vs. Databricks' 15-point boost
bullets.body: Snowflake confirmed AI pass-through revenues are immaterial (~1% of mix), adding only ~1 point to reported growth versus Databricks' ~15-point boost from reselling AI models/compute. UBS views SNOW's reluctance to chase pass-through revs as a positive for revenue quality. PT unchanged at $370 (17.5x CY27E EV/S, 73x EV/FCF). Databricks core growth is 65% (not 80% headline).

bullets.title: HOOD: $2.0B convertible senior notes offering announced; stock -1.5% in pre-market
bullets.body: Robinhood announced a private offering of $2.0B convertible senior notes due 2029 with a $200M greenshoe option. The stock fell ~1.5% in pre-market on dilution concerns. HOOD was up 16.1% last week (+/- -4.4% YTD).

bullets.title: GEV: Chevron-MSFT 20-year PPA uses GE Vernova turbines for Project Kilby (~2.67 GW Texas data center)
bullets.body: Chevron's Energy Forge One LLC signed a 20-year power purchase agreement with Microsoft for Project Kilby, a ~2.67 GW natural gas data center project in West Texas targeting mid-teen returns. The majority of generation will come from GE Vernova turbines; FID expected by end-2026 with first power delivery in 2028. GEV was up 18.0% last week (+69.8% YTD). Baker Hughes separately noted no available manufacturing slots until 2029 given data center demand.

bullets.title: INTC: PT raised to $135 at Mizuho (Neutral); former SK Hynix CEO hired to lead Foundry
bullets.body: Mizuho raised its Intel price target to $135 from $128 while maintaining a Neutral rating. Intel separately appointed Seok-Hee Lee, former SK Hynix CEO, as the new head of its Foundry business — a significant hire signaling renewed seriousness in the foundry push. INTC was up +2.8% in pre-market.

bullets.title: SMCI: GF Securities upgrades to Buy at $48; +5.2% pre-market
bullets.body: GF Securities upgraded Super Micro Computer to Buy from Hold with a $48 price target, sending the stock up 5.2% in pre-market trading on Monday.

bullets.title: NFLX: Acquires Radford Studio Center at $400M (vs. $1.85B 2021 valuation); expanding broadcaster partnerships
bullets.body: Netflix agreed to acquire Radford Studio Center for ~$400M, well below its 2021 sale price of $1.85B. CEO separately signaled intent to add more traditional broadcasters to the platform following the TF1+ deal in France. Netflix denied interest in acquiring Roku (withdrew from bidding per Semafor) or Lionsgate.

bullets.title: PSKY/WBD: Merger clears Canada and South Africa competition reviews; global regulatory approvals ongoing
bullets.body: The Paramount Skydance/Warner Bros. Discovery merger received Canadian Competition Act clearance (statutory waiting period expired June 20) and South African Competition Commission approval (June 19). Deal completion remains subject to regulatory clearance in other jurisdictions; PSKY continuing engagement with antitrust enforcers globally.

bullets.title: RBLX: +19% last week on Grow a Garden 2 launch, Russia ban lift, TTK hit 4M players on launch day
bullets.body: Roblox shares surged 19% last week on improved engagement trends including the Grow a Garden 2 launch, lifting of Russia ban, and summer seasonality tailwind. The new first-person shooter TTK Testing reached 4M players on launch day. JPM notes CCUs held steady over the weekend. Despite last week's rally, RBLX fell -4.4% in pre-market Monday.

bullets.title: DIS: Toy Story 5 delivers $160M opening weekend — best Toy Story franchise debut, +81.9% YoY box office
bullets.body: Disney's Toy Story 5 earned $160M in its opening weekend, making it the best Toy Story franchise opening ever and the top 2026 film debut. The broader US/Canada weekend box office reached $228.1M, up 81.9% YoY. North American summer box office (May 1–Labor Day) is at ~$1.85B, up 16% YoY, nearly matching 2019 levels. Toy Story 5 also led China's weekly box office with CNY121.7M.

bullets.title: T/VZ: UBS 2Q wireless preview — T and TMUS Buy, VZ Neutral; TMUS PT cut to $255 from $300
bullets.body: UBS previews 2Q wireless: industry postpaid phone adds moderate to ~2.0M (vs 2.1M YoY). AT&T (Buy, PT $31) expected to add 358K postpaid phones, 285K fiber adds, $4.4B FCF in 2Q. T-Mobile (Buy, PT cut to $255 from $300 on 13x 27E FCF/sh vs prior 15x) expected to add 270K postpaid accounts and generate $16B in full-year buybacks. Verizon (Neutral, PT $48) expected 123K postpaid adds and 355K broadband adds with new Simplicity plans; 2026 viewed as transition year.
